subject.title: feat(release): preflight all extended-stable npm packages

question: Is the current evidence sufficient to merge a protected npm release workflow change without a linked after-fix run or log showing the new extended-stable plugin pack artifact?
rationale: The code path is reviewable, but the changed surface is release automation and the PR body only states the smoke/static checks rather than giving inspectable real-behavior proof for the new artifact path.

options.title: Require linked artifact proof
options.body: Ask for a workflow run, terminal transcript, or redacted artifact manifest showing the all-publishable plugin tarballs and checksums from this head before merge.

options.title: Accept the stated proof
options.body: A release owner may explicitly accept the PR body's stated smoke/static evidence and rely on exact-head CI plus manual release review.

options.title: Keep branch-bound preflight
options.body: If arbitrary SHA validation-only execution is not desired, pause this PR and keep the existing branch-tip-bound preflight contract.

recommendation.title: Require linked artifact proof
recommendation.body: Ask for a workflow run, terminal transcript, or redacted artifact manifest showing the all-publishable plugin tarballs and checksums from this head before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the merged extended-stable release workflow changes and this follow-up area, so he has the clearest recent context for the release-proof question.
